toc.title: The Scrum Team at a Glance (CSM 1.1)
The Scrum Team's Responsibilities and Accountabilities (CSM 1.1)
How the Three Accountabilities Interact in a Sprint (SF 2.1)
Scrum Team and a Traditional Work Group Compared
Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

html:
1The Scrum Team at a Glance (CSM 1.1)

"The fundamental unit of Scrum is a small team of people, a Scrum Team."

Feature What the Guide says
Composition One Scrum Master, one Product Owner, and Developers. Within a Scrum Team there are no sub-teams or hierarchies
Focus "A cohesive unit of professionals focused on one objective at a time, the Product Goal"
Cross-functional The members have all the skills necessary to create value each Sprint
Self-managing They internally decide who does what, when, and how
Size Small enough to remain nimble, large enough to complete significant work within a Sprint: typically 10 or fewer people. "Smaller teams communicate better and are more productive"
If too large Reorganize into multiple cohesive Scrum Teams, each focused on the same product, sharing the same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner
Responsible for All product-related activities: stakeholder collaboration, verification, maintenance, operation, experimentation, research and development, "and anything else that might be required"
Empowered by the organization "They are structured and empowered by the organization to manage their own work"
Pace "Working in Sprints at a sustainable pace improves the Scrum Team's focus and consistency"
Accountable for "The entire Scrum Team is accountable for creating a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint"

Scrum defines three specific accountabilities within the team: the Developers, the Product Owner and the Scrum Master.

Old wording

The 2017 Guide spoke of a Development Team inside the Scrum Team, of 3 to 9 members ("fewer than three ... decrease interaction", "more than nine members requires too much coordination", not counting the Product Owner and Scrum Master unless they also did the work), and of self-organizing teams. It said Scrum "recognizes no sub-teams in the Development Team", and that "accountability belongs to the Development Team as a whole". The 2020 Guide removed the team within a team: there is one Scrum Team of typically 10 or fewer, self-managing, with no sub-teams or hierarchies.

Exam angle

if an option creates a sub-team (a testing team, a design team, a team lead), adds a hierarchy, or says that a manager assigns work, it contradicts the Guide. If an option says the whole Scrum Team is accountable for the Increment, that is correct.

2Cross-Functional and Self-Managing (SF 2.2)

Term Guide meaning Common misunderstanding
Cross-functional Members have all the skills necessary to create value each Sprint. Scrum engages people who "collectively" have the skills and "share or acquire such skills as needed" It does not mean that everyone can do everything: skills are held by the team as a whole
Self-managing Members internally decide who does what, when, and how It does not mean "no rules" or "no Product Owner": the team works within the framework toward the Product Goal

2.1 Benefits (list at least three) Beyond the Guide

Benefit Why it follows from the design
Fewer hand-offs and dependencies Everything needed to finish an Increment is inside the team, so work does not wait for other groups
Faster decisions and faster adaptation The people who learn something decide immediately. The Guide: adaptation becomes more difficult when people "are not empowered or self-managing"; a Scrum Team adapts "the moment it learns anything new"
Higher quality through shared ownership The whole team is accountable for the Increment, and Developers hold each other accountable
Higher motivation and ownership People choose how to do the work and are respected "to be capable, independent people"
Skill sharing and learning The team "share[s] or acquire[s] such skills as needed", so knowledge spreads and the team is less dependent on single experts
Better collaboration and transparency One team, one goal, one Product Backlog: no competing priorities between sub-groups

3The Developers (CSM 1.3)

"Developers are the people in the Scrum Team that are committed to creating any aspect of a usable Increment each Sprint." The skills needed are broad and vary with the domain of work.

The Guide uses the word "developers" for everyone who does the work: "not to exclude, but to simplify. If you get value from Scrum, consider yourself included." Testers, designers, analysts and other specialists who create the Increment are Developers.

3.1 The Developers are always accountable for

Accountability What it means Covered in
Creating a plan for the Sprint, the Sprint Backlog They select the work and plan how to do it Topics 7 and 11
Instilling quality by adhering to a Definition of Done Quality is built in; work that does not meet the Definition of Done is not part of the Increment Topic 12
Adapting their plan each day toward the Sprint Goal They inspect progress and update the plan, at the Daily Scrum and at other times Topic 8
Holding each other accountable as professionals Peers, not the Scrum Master or a manager, hold the standards Topic 12

3.2 Other Developer duties across the Guide

Duty Where the Guide says it
Select Product Backlog items for the Sprint, in discussion with the Product Owner Sprint Planning, Topic Two
Plan the work; decide how to turn items into Increments, "at the sole discretion of the Developers" Sprint Planning, Topic Three
Size Product Backlog items ("the Developers who will be doing the work are responsible for the sizing") Product Backlog
Conduct the Daily Scrum, choosing its structure and techniques Daily Scrum
Negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog with the Product Owner when the work turns out different, without affecting the Sprint Goal Sprint Goal
Conform to the Definition of Done Definition of Done
Exam angle

the Developers own how the work is done and the plan for the Sprint. They do not own the order of the Product Backlog (the Product Owner) or the effectiveness of the Scrum framework (the Scrum Master).

4The Scrum Team's Responsibilities and Accountabilities (CSM 1.1)

Level Accountable or responsible for
The entire Scrum Team Creating a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint; all product-related activities, including stakeholder collaboration; collaborating on the Sprint Goal; taking part in all events; inspecting and adapting; creating a Definition of Done if the organization has no standard (Topic 12); respecting a sustainable pace
Developers The Sprint Backlog, quality, the daily plan, mutual accountability
Product Owner The value of the product and Product Backlog management (Topic 4)
Scrum Master Establishing Scrum and the team's effectiveness (Topic 5)

5How the Three Accountabilities Interact in a Sprint (SF 2.1)

Moment Product Owner Developers Scrum Master
Sprint Planning Proposes how the product could increase its value; ensures attendees are prepared; helps define the Sprint Goal Select items, plan how to create an Increment that meets the Definition of Done Ensures the event takes place, is positive, productive and timeboxed
During the Sprint Orders and refines the Product Backlog; negotiates scope without endangering the Sprint Goal Create the Increment; hold the Daily Scrum; adapt the plan toward the Sprint Goal Coaches; causes the removal of impediments
Sprint Review Discusses progress toward the Product Goal; the Product Backlog may be adjusted Present the work that is Done Facilitates stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed
Sprint Retrospective Takes part as a member of the Scrum Team Inspect how the Sprint went and agree improvements Takes part as a member; the team's effectiveness is the Scrum Master's accountability

The three work as one team toward one goal: the Product Owner decides what is most valuable, the Developers decide how to build it and how much fits, and the Scrum Master makes sure the framework and the team's effectiveness hold.

6Scrum Team and a Traditional Work Group ComparedBeyond the Guide

Scrum Team Traditional functional group
Structure One team with three accountabilities; no hierarchies Departments with managers and sub-teams
Who assigns work The team decides who does what A manager assigns tasks
Skills Collectively all needed to create the Increment Specialist groups hand work over
Decision-making Product Owner for value and order; Developers for how Escalated up the hierarchy
Accountability The entire team for the Increment Each function for its own step

7Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

  1. No sub-teams, no hierarchies. A "test team", "design team" or "team lead" inside the Scrum Team contradicts the Guide.
  2. Typically 10 or fewer. A larger group should become multiple Scrum Teams that share the same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner. The 2017 "3 to 9" figure is old wording.
  3. Cross-functional means collectively skilled, not "everyone does everything".
  4. Self-managing means the team decides who does what, when and how. An option where a manager, the Product Owner or the Scrum Master assigns tasks is wrong.
  5. The whole Scrum Team is accountable for the Increment. "Only the Developers" or "only the Product Owner" is wrong.
  6. Developers is an inclusive word: it covers all specialists who create the Increment. A person does not need the title "developer".
  7. The Developers decide how. Nobody tells them how to turn Product Backlog items into Increments.
  8. The organization must empower the team. If the team is not empowered to manage its work, the Scrum Master helps the organization see that.
  9. Hold each other accountable is the Developers' job. The Scrum Master coaches; the manager does not discipline within the Scrum framework.
  10. Old wording "Development Team", "self-organizing", "potentially releasable" and a 3 to 9 member range are 2017 terms. Answer from the 2020 wording.

8Exam Q&A

8.1 Scenario questions (choose the best answer)

S1The Developers need database skills that nobody on the team has. A manager proposes a separate "database team" to which the Developers hand over that work. What is the best response?

  • AHelp the Scrum Team share or acquire the skills so that it can finish the work itself
  • BHand the database work over after the Sprint, so that the Sprint is not delayed
  • CCreate a database sub-team inside the Scrum Team with its own lead
  • DMove the database work to the Product Backlog of the other team
Show the answer

Answer: A. A Scrum Team is cross-functional: the members collectively have the skills to create value each Sprint and share or acquire skills as needed. Sub-teams are not allowed inside a Scrum Team, and hand-offs reduce the team's ability to produce an Increment in a Sprint.

S2A Scrum Team has one Product Owner, one Scrum Master and thirteen Developers. Communication is poor and the Daily Scrum takes too long. What does the Guide suggest?

  • AReplace the Scrum Master with a team lead who coordinates the thirteen Developers and takes the decisions
  • BReorganize into multiple cohesive Scrum Teams that share the same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner
  • CSplit the Developers into two sub-teams inside the Scrum Team, each with its own lead who reports to the Scrum Master
  • DAppoint a manager for each group of five Developers so that daily coordination is handled by someone with authority
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Scrum Team is typically ten or fewer people. If it becomes too large, it should consider reorganizing into multiple cohesive Scrum Teams focused on the same product, sharing the same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner. Sub-teams and managers are hierarchies that the Scrum Team does not have.

S3The Developers ask the Product Owner to assign each of them a share of the Sprint Backlog items. What should the Scrum Master do?

  • AAsk the line manager to assign them
  • BAssign the items fairly, because the Scrum Master is accountable for effectiveness
  • CLet the Product Owner decide, since the Product Owner is accountable for value
  • DCoach the Developers to decide among themselves who does what, as a self-managing team
Show the answer

Answer: D. A self-managing Scrum Team decides internally who does what, when and how, and the Scrum Master coaches the team in self-management and cross-functionality. Assignment by the Product Owner, the Scrum Master or a manager takes away that self-management.

S4The Developers propose that the testers form a sub-team with its own lead who approves all test results. Which response matches the Guide?

  • AExplain that a Scrum Team has no sub-teams or hierarchies and that the Developers hold each other accountable for quality
  • BApprove it, because testers need a lead who can sign off the test results before an item counts as Done
  • CAsk the Product Owner to name the lead, because the Product Owner is accountable for the value and the quality of the product
  • DApprove it for the first few Sprints only, and review whether the lead is still needed in the Retrospective
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Guide states that a Scrum Team has no sub-teams or hierarchies, and that the Developers instil quality through the Definition of Done and hold each other accountable as professionals. A lead who approves results adds a hierarchy.

S5After a Sprint in which the Increment did not meet the Definition of Done, a stakeholder asks who is accountable. What is the best answer?

  • AOnly the Developers, because they wrote the code
  • BOnly the Product Owner, because the Product Owner is accountable for the value
  • CThe entire Scrum Team, which is accountable for creating a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint
  • DOnly the Scrum Master, because the Scrum Master is accountable for effectiveness
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Guide says that the entire Scrum Team is accountable for creating a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint, in addition to the three specific accountabilities. The Developers are accountable for adhering to the Definition of Done, but the team as a whole stands behind the Increment.

S6A Developer says: "I am a designer, not a developer, so the Daily Scrum is not for me." What is the best reply?

  • AYou are right: designers are not Developers, so they take part only in the Sprint Review and the Retrospective
  • BDesigners join the Daily Scrum only if they report to a Developer, who speaks for them there
  • CDesigners may attend the Daily Scrum, but only to listen, because only coders do the work of the Increment
  • DDevelopers are all the people committed to creating any aspect of a usable Increment, so you take part
Show the answer

Answer: D. The Guide defines Developers as the people in the Scrum Team who are committed to creating any aspect of a usable Increment each Sprint, and uses the word "developers" to include everyone who gets value from Scrum. A designer who creates part of the Increment is a Developer.

S7Team members of a Scrum Team also receive daily task lists from their department managers, which conflict with the Sprint Backlog. What should the Scrum Master do?

  • AHelp the managers understand that the Scrum Team is empowered to manage its own work, and work with them on the conflict
  • BAsk the Developers to follow the managers' lists first, because the line managers hold the authority over their time and their performance reviews
  • CMerge the managers' lists into the Product Backlog without telling the Product Owner, so the work becomes visible
  • DCancel the Sprint and restart it once the managers have agreed on a single list of tasks for each Developer
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Scrum Team is structured and empowered by the organization to manage its own work, and the Scrum Master serves the organization by helping it understand Scrum and removing barriers. Obeying the lists undermines self-management, adding items silently bypasses the Product Owner, and only the Product Owner could cancel a Sprint, which is not needed here.

S8What is the best summary of what "cross-functional" means in the Guide?

  • AEvery member can do every task, so that any Developer can replace any other at any moment during the Sprint
  • BThe members together have all the skills needed to create value each Sprint
  • CEach member belongs to a different department, so that every function of the organization is represented on the team
  • DThe team includes a representative of every department that has an interest in the product, who report back to it
Show the answer

Answer: B. Cross-functional teams have all the skills necessary to create value in each Sprint, collectively. It does not require that every person can do everything, nor a representative from each department.

S9Which statement describes a benefit of a cross-functional, self-managing Scrum Team?

  • AThe team can finish all work without any stakeholder input, because it already knows what the product should be
  • BThe team no longer needs a Product Owner, because the Developers decide what is valuable among themselves
  • CThe team can create an Increment and adapt quickly without waiting for people outside the team
  • DThe team can ignore the Definition of Done, since members hold each other accountable in other ways
Show the answer

Answer: C. Having all needed skills inside the team and the freedom to decide how to work reduces hand-offs and delays and allows the team to adapt the moment it learns something. The team still collaborates with stakeholders, still has a Product Owner and still follows the Definition of Done.

8.2 Recall Q&As

R1What does a Scrum Team consist of?

Show the answer

One Scrum Master, one Product Owner and Developers. There are no sub-teams or hierarchies.

R2How large is a Scrum Team?

Show the answer

Small enough to be nimble and large enough to complete significant work within a Sprint, typically 10 or fewer people.

R3What should a Scrum Team that has become too large do?

Show the answer

Reorganize into multiple cohesive Scrum Teams focused on the same product, sharing the same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner.

R4What does cross-functional mean?

Show the answer

The members have all the skills necessary to create value each Sprint.

R5What does self-managing mean?

Show the answer

The members internally decide who does what, when and how.

R6On what is the Scrum Team focused?

Show the answer

One objective at a time, the Product Goal.

R7For what is the entire Scrum Team accountable?

Show the answer

Creating a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint.

R8For what is the Scrum Team responsible?

Show the answer

All product-related activities: stakeholder collaboration, verification, maintenance, operation, experimentation, research and development, and anything else required.

R9What are the three accountabilities within the Scrum Team?

Show the answer

The Developers, the Product Owner and the Scrum Master.

R10Who are the Developers?

Show the answer

The people in the Scrum Team who are committed to creating any aspect of a usable Increment each Sprint.

R11What are the Developers always accountable for?

Show the answer

Creating the Sprint plan (the Sprint Backlog); instilling quality by adhering to a Definition of Done; adapting their plan each day toward the Sprint Goal; holding each other accountable as professionals.

R12Name at least three benefits of a cross-functional, self-managing Scrum Team.

Show the answer

Fewer hand-offs and dependencies; faster decisions and adaptation; higher quality through shared ownership; higher motivation and ownership; skill sharing and learning; better collaboration.

R13How does the 2017 Guide's team size differ from the 2020 Guide?

Show the answer

2017: a Development Team of 3 to 9 members. 2020: a Scrum Team of typically 10 or fewer people.

9Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Composition 1 Scrum Master + 1 Product Owner + Developers; no sub-teams, no hierarchies
Size Typically 10 or fewer; too large → several Scrum Teams with the same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner
Focus One objective at a time: the Product Goal
Cross-functional All skills needed to create value each Sprint (collectively)
Self-managing Decides who does what, when and how
Accountable Entire Scrum Team: a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint
Responsible All product-related activities
Developers Anyone committed to creating any aspect of a usable Increment each Sprint
Developers always Sprint Backlog · Definition of Done · daily adaptation toward the Sprint Goal · mutual accountability
Developers decide How to turn items into Increments (sole discretion)
Empowerment The organization structures and empowers the team to manage its own work
Pace Sprints at a sustainable pace improve focus and consistency
Old wording Development Team, self-organizing, 3 to 9 members (2017)
